question: does the Groebner-Shirshov filtration grading -- the jet vertical degree, indexed by Coxeter length of the normal-form word -- separate magic from non-magic nucleon configurations?
why_distinct_from_q_degree: symbolic_nf_q_degree_magic_probe measured degree in q; this measures the filtration by NF word length, a different grading

ceiling.note: unconditional arithmetic; NOT an exclusion of many-body structure. The GS word-length grading is NOT the bond-product grading -- see grading_identification: different cardinality (4 vs C(A,2)+1) and the folding is many-to-one on bond count. QOU.Mass.BodyOrderJetGrading.body_eq_graded IS discharged for the bond-product model by body_eq_graded_of_bond_product; an earlier draft of this probe wrongly called it assumed, and wrongly claimed the two models index in opposite directions (the complement bijection esymm_eq_compl_sum absorbs that).

grading_identification.question: is the GS word-length filtration (0..3) identifiable with the bond-product / Mayer grading (0..|s|)?
grading_identification.answer: no -- different cardinality, and the folding loses bond count

control: exhaustive at each level: every Z in 0..A
arithmetic: exact over Q (fractions.Fraction); no float, no evaluation at any numerical q
